analysis.title: Positioning Mondays - Week 45
key_insights: Degrossing accelerated to its highest velocity since July in dollar terms, per GS Prime Brokerage. Long sales outpaced short covers 5 to 1.

Fundamental L/S net leverage and the Fundamental L/S ratio are at 1-, 3- and 5-year lows. US Fundamental L/S gross and net leverage had their largest weekly declines since Covid and Liberation Day respectively.
Global equities were net sold (-1.0 SD, 1-year). Single stocks were net sold for an 8th straight week, while macro products were net bought for a 3rd straight week.
8 of 11 global sectors were net sold, led by Info Tech, Industrials and Energy. Real Estate, Utilities and Materials were the only net bought sectors.

The GS floor was a moderate net seller of long-only flow on the week, with a steady stream of semiconductor supply. It has net sold more than $30bn of Tech (TMT + Comm Services) since the unwind began, versus -$21bn in the July episode.
CTAs sold over $11.6bn of SPX and $3bn of NDX over 5 days. Another $31bn of SPX and $2.9bn of NDX is modelled to be sold over the next 5 sessions.
Retail demand was the weakest since last June, with 2 significant daily sell skews on the week. The desk said Thursday had the makings of a capitulation event.

Equity mutual funds still saw large inflows: +$89bn on the week (+$37bn US) and +$265bn over 4 weeks ($111bn US). Technology funds had the largest inflows, though the data do not capture moves after the US midterm elections.
Corporate buybacks are accelerating as companies exit blackout windows. About 90% of the S&P 500 is in an open window, with about 93% expected by the end of the week.
The desk flags oil and yields as down, and says vol needs to keep stabilizing before capital is redeployed. US CPI is the next macro focus.
Europe saw risk-off flows for a 4th straight week. The GS book is overweight Europe vs MSCI World by 3.25% and underweight North America by 13.91%.
Sentiment is bearish: AAII bears are 48.4% against a 31% historical average, CNN Fear & Greed is 24/100 (Extreme Fear), and the GS Sentiment Indicator bounced to +0.6 from +0.2.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The desk names the US CPI print due the day after the note (10 Nov) as the next macro focus. No figure is given.

risk_factors: Continued CTA selling, with the baseline taking the position to net short within a month.
Weak retail demand and ongoing semiconductor supply.
Vol has not yet stabilized enough for capital to be redeployed, per the desk.
vol_and_positioning: Overall book gross leverage rose 0.1 pts to 314.2% (85th percentile, 1-year). Net leverage fell 1.8 pts to 71.8% (4th percentile, 1-year). Overall book L/S ratio fell 1.2% to 1.592 (3rd percentile, 1-year).
Fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 6.2 pts to 205.8% (19th percentile, 1-year). Net leverage fell 4.1 pts to 45.3% (2nd percentile, 5-year).
Beta-adjusted Fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 13.1 pts to 216.5% (22nd percentile, 3-year). Beta-adjusted net leverage fell 7.6 pts to 57.2% (4th percentile, 3-year).

CTA signals are negative in 50-60% of global equity markets at short and medium-term horizons, including the S&P. The baseline expects $23bn of SPX futures sold over 1 week and $45bn over 1 month, which would take the position to net short. Relevant S&P trigger levels are about 7675 (short-term) and 7549 (medium-term).
Asset managers were tiny net buyers of S&P futures in the week ending 3 Nov (CFTC).
The 4 Nov week saw 33% open-market flow vs 67% 10b5-1 flow on the GS buyback desk, against 22%/78% the week before.

tension_points.bull_case: Equity mutual funds still saw +$89bn of inflows. Buybacks are accelerating as about 90% of the S&P 500 exits blackout, with $1.5T of 2026 authorizations. The desk said Thursday had the makings of a capitulation event.
tension_points.bear_case: Hedge fund degrossing is at its fastest since July and Fundamental L/S net leverage is at multi-year lows. CTAs are modelled to sell $23bn of SPX futures over the next week, taking the position to net short within a month. Retail demand is weak.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The desk says vol needs to continue to stabilize for capital to be redeployed. CTA flow estimates update as prices move relative to the 7675 and 7549 S&P levels.
